# shopify_collection (Resource)

A collection: title, handle, description, sort order and which products it holds, by hand (`product_ids`) or by rules (`conditions`). **A poor fit for Terraform unless you bootstrap a store or keep a few collections in a repository:** collections back navigation, but their texts and products are edited in the admin all the time, and every admin edit to a managed attribute is reverted on the next apply. Attributes you leave unset are not managed; the rules of a smart collection suit Terraform best. Membership is managed for collections with at most one non-shareable conditions source, which every collection made in the admin, with the older API or by this provider has. That includes a source another app created; Shopify may reject changes to it. Collections with several sources, a sub-collection or shareable source, variant-level selections or a condition Shopify can't express as input are read without membership: setting `match_type`, `conditions` or `product_ids` for them fails. Exclusions, the product order of `MANUAL` collections, the image, publishing and metafields are not managed. Destroying a collection deletes it with its publications and translations; the products stay. Menu items pointing at it lose their target, so add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to collections that back navigation. A collection that already has the handle, such as `frontpage` which every store has, needs `adopt_existing = true`; destroy then leaves it in place. Import with the handle.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `handle` (String) The collection's URL handle, unique per shop. Changing it renames the collection in place and creates no URL redirect. Lower case, no whitespace: Shopify lower-cases anything else.
- `title` (String) The collection title.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing collection with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `conditions` (String) The rules of a smart collection: a JSON list of [`CollectionSourceInclusionConditionInput`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2026-10/input-objects/CollectionSourceInclusionConditionInput) objects in the API's camelCase, one key each, written with `jsonencode([...])`, for example `{ productTag = { relation = "TAGGED_WITH", values = ["sale"], matchType = "ANY" } }`. Shopify validates kinds and values. Order matters; amounts and values compare numerically, so `"5"` matches Shopify's `"5.0"`. Reference metafield definitions and metaobjects by their resource or data source IDs, which differ per store. Products match asynchronously, so a new rule can take a moment to fill the collection. `jsonencode([])` removes all conditions. Unset means unmanaged. A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `description_html` (String) The description as HTML. Shopify repairs malformed HTML; the configured text is kept while Shopify still holds what it returned at the last apply, so the repair is no diff, but a later admin edit is. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `match_type` (String) `ALL` or `ANY`: whether a product must match all `conditions` or any of them. Required when `conditions` is a non-empty list. Null for a collection without a source. Unset means unmanaged. Null when the collection's membership can't be managed (see the resource description). A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `product_ids` (Set of String) Product GIDs included by hand, whatever the conditions say. Reference `shopify_product` IDs, so products are created first and their GIDs never sit in the configuration. A product deleted elsewhere drops out and shows as drift. `[]` removes them all. Unset means unmanaged. Null when the collection's membership can't be managed (see the resource description). A source another app created is managed too, but Shopify may reject changes to it.
- `seo_description` (String) Search engine description. Null while Shopify uses the collection description. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `seo_title` (String) Search engine title. Null while Shopify uses the collection title. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `sort_order` (String) How products are sorted: `ALPHA_ASC`, `ALPHA_DESC`, `BEST_SELLING`, `MOST_RELEVANT`, `CREATED`, `CREATED_DESC`, `MANUAL`, `PRICE_ASC` or `PRICE_DESC`. A new collection gets `MOST_RELEVANT` when this is unset. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `template_suffix` (String) Theme template suffix, such as `special` for `collection.special.json`. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Collection GID.
- `source_id` (String) The `CollectionConditionsSource` GID that holds `match_type`, `conditions` and `product_ids`; null while the collection has none. The first condition or product creates it, and removing the last one deletes it.
